title: NCR Transportation
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE This is a Sources Sought Notice (SSN) ONLY. The government seeks to procure a non-personnel services contract to provide ground transportation for family members of U.S. Army Soldiers in and around the National Capital Region (NCR) area. The NCR encompasses Washington, DC; Montgomery and Prince George's Counties in Maryland; Arlington, Fairfax, Loudoun, and Prince William Counties in Virginia; and the incorporated cities of Alexandria, Falls Church, Fairfax, and Manassas in Virginia. The contractor must be registered with the Defense Travel Management Office (DTMO Approved Carrier Listing (ACL) to be considered for the award. A small business set-aside will be considered, provided two (2) or more qualified small businesses respond to this sources sought notice with information sufficient to support a set-aside. Be advised that the U.S. Government will not be able to set aside this requirement if two (2) or more small businesses do not respond with information to support the set-aside. We encourage all small businesses, in all socioeconomic categories (including, 8(a) Business Development Program, Small Disadvantage Business, Historically Underutilized Business Zone, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned, Women-Owned Small Business concerns), to identify their capabilities in meeting the requirement at a fair market price. This notice is issued solely for information and planning purposes � it does not constitute a Request for Quote (RFQ)/Invitation for Bid (IFB)/Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFQ, IFB or RFP in the future. This notice does not commit the U.S. Government to contract for any supply or service. Further, the U.S. Government is not seeking quotes, bids or proposals at this time and will not accept unsolicited proposals in response to this sources sought notice. The U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this notice. Submittals will not be returned to the responder. Not responding to this notice does not preclude participation in any future RFQ or IFB or RFP, if any is issued. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on the Government-wide Point of Entry. It is the responsibility of potential offerors to monitor the Government-wide Point of Entry for additional information pertaining to this requirement. The anticipated NAICS code(s) is/are: 485999-All Other Transit and Ground Passenger Transportation Attached is the draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) for details. Responses to this Sources Sought Notice shall be e-mailed to the Contract Specialist, Zachery E Reynolds, at zachery.e.reynolds.civ@army.mil and the Contracting Officer, Deborah R Davis-Maxwell, at deborah.r.davis-maxwell.civ@army.mil, no later than 14 September 2026 at 10:00a.m. EST (Fort Knox local time). Limitations on subcontracting and nonmanufacturer rule do not apply to small business set-asides for contracts at or below the Simplified Acquisition Threshold (SAT). It does apply to 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, EDWOSB, and WOSB set asides regardless of the dollar value of the award. Small business contractors awarded contracts above the SAT are required to comply with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting when utilizing subcontractors. The penalty for non-compliance is the greater of (A) $500K or (B) the dollar amount expended, in excess of permitted levels. See FAR 52.219-14 - Limitations on Subcontracting for Small Business. In response to this sources sought, please provide: Name of the firm, point of contact, phone number, email address, UEI number, CAGE code, a statement regarding small business status (including small business type(s)/certifications(s) such as SDB, 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, WOSB, etc.) and the corresponding NAICS code. Identify whether your firm is interested in competing for this requirement as a prime contractor or not. Identify subcontracting, joint ventures or teaming arrangement that will be pursued, if any. Information in sufficient detail regarding previous experience (indicate whether as a prime contractor or subcontractor) on similar requirements (include size, scope, complexity, timeframe, government or commercial), pertinent certifications, etc., that will facilitate making a capability determination. The information must clearly explain how your firm can satisfy the requirements as outlined in the PWS. General statements of interest will not be used as a capability determination. Information to help determine if the requirement is commercially available, including pricing information, basis for the pricing information (e.g., market pricing, catalog pricing), delivery schedules, customary terms and conditions, warranties, etc. Identify how the Army can best structure these contract requirements to facilitate competition by and among small business concerns. Identify any condition or action that may be having the effect of unnecessarily restricting competition with respect to this acquisition. Please contact the MICC Advocate for Competition, Scott Kukes, at scott.d.kukes.civ@army.mil or 520-944-7373, if you believe that this action is unreasonably restricting competition. Include the subject of the acquisition, this announcement, and the MICC POC information from the notice. Provide the specific aspects that unreasonably restrict competition and the rationale for such conclusion.

title: FLORIDA NATIONAL CEMETERY CHEMICALS
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial services prepared in accordance with FAR part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested, and a written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 36C78626Q0116 is issued as a request for quotation (RFQ). This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. Quoters are responsible for obtaining all amendments or additional information concerning this announcement at Sam.gov. NORTH AMERICAN INDUSTRIAL CLASSIFICATION SYSTEM (NAICS) CODE: This acquisition is set-aside for is set aside for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSBs). The NAICS code for this procurement is 325320 � Pesticide and Other Agricultural Chemical Manufacturing. The business size standard number of employees is 1,150 Employees. This notice shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government to ultimately award a contract, nor does it restrict the Government to a particular acquisition approach. The U.S. Department of Veteran Affairs, National Cemetery Administration (NCA), anticipates the award of Firm Fixed price. This Firm Fixed Contract is for Florida National Cemetery, SW 102nd Bushnell, FL 33513. ANTICIPATED PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: Base Year: September 21, 2026 � September 30, 2026 RESPONSE TO REQUEST FOR QUOTE (RFQ): Quotes are due to the Administrative Contracting Officer, no later than 10:00am on September 14, 2026. Responses to this announcement will result in a Firm Fixed Contract. The Government intends to make award without discussions. All information submitted in response to this announcement is voluntary and the Government will not pay for information provided nor will it compensate any respondent for any cost incurred in developing information provided for the Government. Quoters are responsible for obtaining and acknowledging all amendments or additional information concerning this announcement at SAM.gov. SOLICITATION QUESTIONS: All questions regarding this solicitation are to be submitted to the Contract Specialists via email no later than close of business, September 8, 2026. Questions pertaining to this announcement shall be sent by email to: Janice.Brooks@va.gov and copy (cc) Larry.Curtis@va.gov. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted. Associated answers to questions submitted will be provided via a solicitation amendment. If Quoter fails to endorse amendment(s), quote will be considered non-responsive and ineligible for award. INSTRUCTIONS TO QUOTERS: Interested quoters MUST be registered with the SAM at http://www.sam.gov and must compete the Online Representations and Certifications Application (ORCA) at http://www.sam.gov prior to the solicitation closing date. Failure to comply will result in the quoter being considered Non-Responsive. Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) and Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB) socio-economic category concerns MUST have an active/current registration with https://veterans.certify.sba.gov/. Failure to comply will result in the quoter being considered Non-Responsive and ineligible for award. Interested Quoters who do not have a current/active SAM account registration or who are not certified as a Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business or certified as a Veterans Owned Small Business in the SBA website (veterans.certify.sba.gov) upon solicitation close date will be considered Non-responsive and ineligible for award. All quotes are to be submitted to Administrative Contracting Officer, via email at Janice.Brooks@va.gov and copy (cc) Larry.Curtis@va.gov no later than 10:00am EST on September 14, 2026. IT IS THE RESPONSIBILITY OF THE QUOTER TO SUBMIT THEIR BEST QUOTE AT THE TIME QUOTES ARE DUE. LATE QUOTES MAY NOT BE CONSIDERED. EVALUATION PROCESS: The Government intends to award a Firm Fixed Contract resulting from this Solicitation to the responsible Quoter whose quote provides the best benefit to the Government, price and other factors considered. The following factors shall be used to evaluate quotes: Lowest Price that meets the Chemicals Salient Characteristics. Salient Characteristics are defined as containing the same active ingredient(s), and same concentrations that must be met for a chemical to be considered brand name or equal. EVALUATION METHODOLOGY: In accordance with FAR Overhaul 12.203(C)(2) the Government will award a firm fixed price contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible Quoter whose quote will be the most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered. Award shall be made based on the lowest evaluated price meeting acceptability standards for non-cost factors. The quoter must be compliant with all the solicitation�s general requirements. General Requirements consist of chemicals products meeting standards. See attached Documents before submitting a proposal: 1. "36C78626Q0116 - Combined Solicitation Far Overhaul - CHEMICALS FLORIDA NATIONAL CEMETERY" 2. A - Statement of Work Florida National Cemetery Chemicals. 3. B - Price Schedule. See attached solicitation Amendment.

title: Court Reporting, Certified Summarized or Verbatim Transcription
description: This is a Sources Sought Notice issued solely for information and planning purposes (market research) pursuant to FAR Part 10. This notice does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or Request for Quotation (RFQ), nor does it guarantee a future solicitation. The Government is seeking capability statements from qualified Small Business concerns. Although this requirement is primarily planned as a 100% Small Business set-aside, expressions of interest from other socioeconomic categories (e.g., 8(a), SDVOSB, WOSB, HUBZone) will be evaluated to establish the optimal procurement strategy. Scope of Work & Task Requirements: The requirement shall include the following tasks Task 1 � The service provider shall provide court reporter services at hearings. Task 2 � The service provider shall provide verbatim legal transcription of all audio files. Task 3 � The service provider shall ensure all transcription work is conducted within the United States. Task 4 -- The service provider shall not include names of witnesses or interviewees on any external documents. Task 5 � The service provider shall identify speakers throughout the documents. Task 6- The service provider shall provide an initial TRANSCRIPT via electronic copy (.pdf) of each hearing to the Virginia Air National Guard Legal Office for authentication no later than 30 calendar days of the completion of the hearing. Task 7 - After authentication, the service provider shall provide the Virginia Air National Guard Legal Office with one final hard copy (paper) and one final electronic copy (.pdf), within 14 calendar days. Task 8 - The service provider shall ensure transcripts are maintained in strict confidence and free from unauthorized disclosure. Task 9 - The service provider shall turn over physical audio files after each call to the COR. Interested sources must submit a capability statement demonstrating their ability to fulfill the operational requirements outlined in this notice. Submissions must address the following elements: Company Profile and Administrative Information: Provide the company's full legal business name, physical address, point of contact details (name, email, phone number), CAGE Code, and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) registered in SAM.gov. Business Size and Socioeconomic Status: Clearly identify business size and all socioeconomic certifications under NAICS code 561492 (e.g., Small Business, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business [SDVOSB], Woman-Owned Small Business [WOSB], 8(a) Program Participant, or HUBZone). Technical Capability and Personnel Qualifications: Describe your firm's core qualifications, including experience providing certified court reporters for live military/legal hearings, verbatim legal transcription proficiency, quality control processes, and capacity to consistently meet the 30-day draft and 14-day final delivery schedules.

The Chemical Process and Nuclear Measurements Group is seeking a semiconductor-grade Process Residual Gas Analyzer (RGA) for use on flow systems, including an ALD reactor, as part of a CHIPS R&D Metrology program. title: SIMStation GO Mobile Simulation Audiovisual Recording and Debriefing System (Notice of Intent to sole source)
description: Acquisition Description & Justification: This is a Notice of Intent, not a request for proposal. The National Institute of Health, Clinical Center (NIH-CC) intends to negotiate on an other than full and open competition basis with SimStation Inc. The NIH Clinical Center Simulation Program requires a portable, self-contained audiovisual (AV) recording and debriefing system to support simulation-based education, clinical training, competency assessment, and in-situ simulation activities throughout the NIH Clinical Center. Simulation activities are conducted in both dedicated simulation spaces and clinical environments where permanently installed AV infrastructure may not be available or practical. Accordingly, the required system must be capable of rapid deployment between locations while providing an integrated capability for audiovisual capture, observation, recording, patient-monitor capture, control, playback, and video-assisted debriefing. The required system must minimize equipment footprint, setup time, cabling, and dependence on permanent AV or NIH network infrastructure while providing a standardized and reliable simulation recording and debriefing workflow. NIH's determination to sole source to SimStation Inc. is based upon the totality of the market research and technical evaluation performed. Alternative commercial and integrated AV solutions were identified and considered. These alternatives provide various portions of the functionality required by the Clinical Center; therefore, NIH does not assert that individual features such as video recording, debriefing, portability, patient-monitor capture, or network independence are unique to SIMStation GO. Rather, SIMStation GO was determined to meet the required combination of operational characteristics in a single purpose-built platform, including: One-case portability; One-person deployment and operation; Rapid setup for in-situ simulation; Integrated audiovisual recording and debriefing; Patient-monitor capture; Dedicated control, debriefing, and viewing capability; Local processing and storage; Non-cloud-based routine operation; No requirement for public internet or NIH enterprise network connectivity during routine simulation activities; Reduced dependence on permanent AV and network infrastructure; and Successful evaluation within the NIH Clinical Center simulation environment. The NIH Clinical Center's virtual and on-site evaluation provided direct evidence that SIMStation GO is suitable for the intended operational environment. In addition, SIMStation Inc. has formally certified that it is the sole-source provider for the proprietary SIMStation GO system and maintains exclusive rights to its firmware, software, and hardware configurations. Place of Performance or Delivery: POP: 9/18/2026 � 09/17/2027 Place of Performance: NIH Clinical Center in Bethesda, MD The statutory authority for this sole source requirement is 41 U.S.C. 1901 (a) (1) as implemented by FAR 13.106-1 only one responsible source and no other supply of service will satisfy agency requirements. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. All responsible sources that could provide the required may submit a capability statement that will be considered by email (subject line to reference NOI-26-008057) by 10:00 AM eastern standard time on 09/14/2026 to: lu-chang.lu@nih.gov All responses received by the closing date of this synopsis will be considered by the Government. A determination not to compete this requirement, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the Government. The purchase order that shall be awarded for this project shall use standard government terms and conditions.

title: Netherlands – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – Financiële Applicatie
description: Met deze aanbesteding beoogt Aanbestedende dienst een leverancier te contracteren voor de levering, implementatie en beheer van één financieel systeem volgens het SaaS-principe met bijbehorende dienstverlening. Dit betekent dat de applicatie niet lokaal op de systemen van Aanbestedende dienst draait maar extern op de servers bij de te contracteren leverancier. De belangrijkste specificaties van het nieuw te leveren financieel systeem zijn: • De applicatie is een zgn. Software as a Service (SaaS) applicatie; • De applicatie kan worden voorzien van (geautomatiseerde) koppelingen met overige door Aanbestedende dienst gebruikte systemen. De overeenkomst bestaat uit de implementatieperiode en de beheerperiode. De implementatieperiode start na ondertekening van de overeenkomst door beide partijen en eindigt na acceptatie van de implementatie waarna de beheerperiode aanvangt. De geplande ingangsdatum van de beheerperiode is 1 januari 2028. De looptijd van de overeenkomst is bepaald op 4 jaar en eindigt derhalve op 31 december 2031. Aanbestedende dienst heeft het recht de duur van de overeenkomst eenzijdig 4 keer te verlengen met een periode van 2 jaar. De totale duur van de overeenkomst zal maximaal 12 jaar bedragen. De overeenkomst eindigt aan het einde van de looptijd van rechtswege, op 31 december 2039.

title: The Supply of Bespoke Blank White Access Control Legic Smart Cards
description: Unite Procurement UK Limited (part of Unite Holding SE), on behalf of the Ministry of Defence, is seeking suppliers to join the Unite Procurement Platform to support the supply of bespoke blank white access control legic smart cards. Requirement Details The procurement covers the following products and services: BESPOKE Blank White Access Control Legic Smart Cards Encoded High-security smart cards with Legic encoding capability for access control systems. Cards must be blank white CR80 format with full encoding functionality. SISYS Blank White CR80 ISO Standard PVC ID Cards (100 pack) ISO/IEC 7810 ID-1 compliant blank PVC cards in white, supplied in packs of 100. Suitable for printing and encoding applications. The Unite Procurement Platform (Unite | Simplify indirect procurement with our smarter platform) offers a compliant route to market for UK Public Sector organisations to manage low-value, high-volume procurement. How to Apply Interested suppliers should register their interest by contacting Unite Procurement UK Limited and provide details of their product range, modification capabilities, and maintenance services. Further information on the onboarding process for the Unite Procurement Platform will be provided upon expression of interest and can also be found at the link attached. Unite Procurement UK Limited does not intend to appoint a sole supplier for this requirement. Instead, multiple suppliers may be onboarded to the Unite Procurement Platform to ensure a diverse and competitive supply base, supporting flexibility and choice for the Ministry of Defence and associated organisations. Suppliers are encouraged to express their interest by the stated closing date to ensure early consideration. However, applications to join the Unite Procurement Platform will be welcome at any time beyond the initial deadline. Unite Procurement UK Limited reserves the right to review and onboard new suppliers on a rolling basis to meet evolving requirements and to maintain a dynamic and responsive supplier network. Contact For any enquiries and interest, please email defence.support@unite.eu with the subject title TSS 790 Opportunity.

title: Emergent Drug Panel-Version 2 (EDP-V2) Kit
description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention intends to award a sole source firm fixed price contract to Cayman Chemical Company, Inc. for the design, manufacture, distribution, and associated laboratory support services for the Emergent Drug Panel-Version 2 (EDP-V2) Kit, a new product line addition within CDC's Traceable Opioid Material (TOM�) Kit program, and continued distribution, product support, and data collection services for existing Emergent Drug Panel (EDP) Kit products. The anticipated period of performance is 09/30/2026 through 09/29/2027. The requirement will include four option years for design and manufacture of additional kits as well as continuous distribution. The Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority of FAR 12.102(a). CDC requires a contractor to: 1. Design and manufacture EDP-V2 kits containing reference materials for emerging synthetic opioids and related drugs of concern (including synthetic opioids, novel benzodiazepines, synthetic cathinones, and related novel psychoactive substances) contributing to the opioid epidemic, meeting or exceeding Current Good Manufacturing Practice (cGMP) standards; 2. Obtain and maintain a DEA exemption/registration status enabling distribution of controlled and non-controlled reference materials to CDC-approved laboratories; 3. Distribute EDP-V2 kits and all other existing EDP Kit product lines to approved laboratories nationally; 4. Provide ongoing product support, customer service, and technical assistance to recipient laboratories for all EDP Kit products; 5. Collect, maintain, and report kit distribution and use-case metrics to CDC in accordance with OMB-approved data collection requirements; and 6. Conduct stability testing on existing EDP Kit materials nearing expiration to determine potential for shelf-life extension. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive quotations; however, all quotations/responses received prior to the date and time below will be considered by the government. NOTE: Interested vendors must clearly provide evidence of their capability to be considered. A determination by the government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Any quotation/response should be emailed to the Contracting Officer at xur0@cdc.gov by 11:00AM (ET) on 09/14/2026.

title: CGC ALEX HALEY THORDON RUDDER BEARING
description: Combined Synopsis/Solicitation - 70Z08526Q0028275 CGC ALEX HALEY availability requires procurement of Government-furnished equipment (GFE) to support Work Item 37, Rudder Stock Remove, Inspect, & Repair. This procurement provides the GFE lower rudder bearings required to support removal, inspection, repair, and reassembly of the port and starboard rudders and rudder stocks. The required GFE consists of the parts identified in 3.0 Required Parts, specifically two Thordon lower bearings, approximately 18.4-inch outside diameter by 15.4-inch inside diameter by 38.1-inch long, Part Number F6875573087. These bearings are required to support the rudder stock lower bearing assembly work and may be installed in place of existing equipment if bearing renewal is directed or required based on inspection results. Timely procurement and availability of these GFE bearings is critical to support rudder removal, rudder stock inspection, upper bearing repairs, lower bearing inspection, rudder reassembly, alignment, operational testing, and completion of the work item during the scheduled availability. QTY: 2 P/N: F6875573087 Thordon Lower Bearing Approx 18.4in OD x 15.4in ID x 38.1in Long NO SUBSTITUTIONS Delivery Address: ATTN: CWO2 Chris Giboney, LCDR Hannah DelGuercio, LT Chris Maytum JAG ALASKA INC. DBA: JAG ALASKA INC 3306 SORREL RD SEWARD, AK, 99664, US Required period of performance: Work must be completed within 10 days of contract award. The Government will award a contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible offeror whose quote conforming to the solicitation is most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered. The following factors will be used to evaluate offers: � Technical Capability (Pass/Fail) � Past Performance (Pass/Fail) � Total Price A quotation must receive an Acceptable rating for all non-price factors to be eligible for award. Among all acceptable quotations, award will be made to the responsible offeror submitting the lowest evaluated price. To establish Technical Capability (Pass/Fail), the quotation must demonstrate a clear understanding of the work statement requirements, conform strictly to all specifications in the attached Statement of Work, and provide any adequate capability and corporate experience documentation required by the solicitation. Failure to meet these criteria will render the quotation unacceptable. The Government will evaluate recent (completed within the last three years) and relevant past performance to assess the likelihood of successful performance. Past performance will be evaluated on an acceptable or unacceptable basis. To receive an acceptable rating, past performance must demonstrate a rating of satisfactory or higher performance of similar work. Offerors without recent or relevant past performance will be assessed as "Neutral" and considered acceptable for award. Past performance demonstrating marginal or below performance is unacceptable. Offerors shall identify all subcontractors anticipated to perform work under this contract. For each subcontractor, the offeror shall provide the subcontractor�s name, address, point of contact, phone number, the specific work items/specifications they will perform, and the percentage of work they will execute. Submit offers electronically via email to the points of contact identified in this notice. The Government does not prescribe a specific quotation format. Offerors must submit a quotation that clearly identifies the items offered and demonstrates compliance with the stated requirements. Submissions must be complete, clear, and presented in a format that allows effective evaluation by the Government. Submit all questions via email to the points of contact identified in this notice. The Government will not accept telephone inquiries. Submit offers on a firm-fixed-price basis. Prices must be all-inclusive and must cover all costs associated with providing the services, including but not limited to labor, materials, equipment, supervision, transportation, and any other costs. The Government may consider offers nonresponsive if they include conditional pricing, price escalation language, or statements indicating that prices are subject to adjustment based on future costs or fees. The Government intends to evaluate offers and make award without discussions; therefore, offerors should submit their best offer with initial submission. The Statement of Work, market research report, and the list of applicable FAR provisions and clauses are attached to this notice.

The attached draft Statement of Work (SOW) establishes the minimum requirement for the upgrade of AFATS 02-02 (P/N 8230001-0501), and training on the maintenance, calibration, programming, and use of said test stand. The test stand will primarily be used to test fuel flow proportioners and float valves in accordance with their relevant Technical Orders (T.O.�s), but will also be used as needed to test refueling receptacles, transfer pumps and other similar components as per their relevant T.O.�s. The following also includes the minimum requirement for the upgrade of a currently nonfunctional calibration cart (P/N: 8231300-0501) for use in calibrating flowmeters and electrical parameters on this system and other existing AFATS configurations. title: Professional Painting & Paper Conservation Services for the National Museum of the Marine Corps

title: Notice of Intent for NIH/NCATS Slurm Slinky Licenses
description: THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE CONTRACT, NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES. A REQUEST FOR QUOTE (RFQ) WILL NOT BE ISSUED AND QUOTES WILL NOT BE REQUESTED. The National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences (NCATS) intends to award a firm fixed price sole source contract under the authority of FAR 12.102(a), only one source being available to meet the Government's needs, to: SchedMD LLC 900 N 100 E Lehi, UT 84043 NCATS hereby submits a notice of intent to award a sole source firm fixed price purchase order for Slurm Slinky Licenses and Support which includes associated maintenance, upgrades, and technical support, for a twelve (12) month period of performance commencing within thirty (30) days of award. The purpose of this acquisition is to obtain software, support, and integration capabilities for Slurm and Slinky Bridge. Slurm is an open-source tool that manages and schedules computing workloads across large computing systems. The support includes Slurm Support Level 3 for 12 months supporting up to 256 computing nodes and graphics processing units, Slurm Slinky Bridge which provides the capability to integrate between local computing systems and cloud resources. Also consulting support from a senior engineer , remote support sessions (8 hours total) and review of system setup and configuration. SchedMD is the original developer, maintainer, and sole commercial support provider for the Slurm Workload Manager. SchedMD is also the exclusive provider of Slinky Bridge, the proprietary software required to integrate Slurm-managed on-premises computing resources with cloud environments. The National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences is building a modern scientific computing environment to support advanced data analysis and large-scale research. This environment is essential for accelerating the development of new treatments, improving drug discovery, and advancing scientific innovation. Researchers use advanced methods such as machine learning, large-scale data analysis, and other data-intensive techniques that require powerful computing systems. These systems include a mix of local and cloud-based computing resources that must work together efficiently. Slurm, combined with Slinky Bridge, enables this hybrid computing approach by managing workloads and allowing jobs to run seamlessly across both environments. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 531210 Software Publisher business size $47M. The period of performance will be for one (1) 12-month base period from date of award. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals, and no solicitation document exists for the requirement. This hereby constitutes a synopsis of the requirement. CLOSING STATEMENT The determination not to compete this proposed contract action is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. The Government will not be responsible for any costs incurred by responding to this notice. This is NOT a request for quotes or proposals. Questions or comments to this Notice of Intent should be directed to the Primary Point of Contact Leah L. Hinson via e-mail only Leah.Hinson@hhs.gov (no phone calls/voice mail). Messages regarding questions will not be accepted and will not receive a response). Please indicate in the subject of your email: Notice of Intent Question Submission � PCA-NCATS�06792 Slurm Slinky Licenses and Support. title: Z2DA--589A7-23-306 Renovate Bldg. 5 & 5B for Mental Health FY27 NRM
description: Project # 589A7-23-306 Renovate 5 & 5B for Mental Health The Department of Veterans Affairs, Network Contracting Office (NCO) 15, has a requirement for Renovate 5 & 5B for Mental Health, project number 589A7-23-306, located at the U.S Department of Veterans Affairs, Robert J. Dole VA Medical Center 5500 E Kellogg Dr, Wichita, KS 67218 The following narrative is intended to provide an overview of the scope of work for the proposed project. Period of Performance 210 calendar days after Notice to Proceed (NTP) Scope of Work Contractor shall perform construction and renovation of the existing space in Building 5 &/or 5B at the Robert J. Dole VA Medical Center campus. This project will prepare approximately 1,100 SF of existing space in building 5 and/or 5B for use as a same day access mental health clinic in adherence to VHA directive 1231(2) & VHA Handbook 1160.1. This project shall be executed in a manner, following the sequence defined in the design narrative, to maintain continuous operations of adjacent VA clinical functions and medical center functionality throughout construction. All construction work shall be performed in full compliance with the complete set of bidding documents, including all contract drawings, specifications, and design narratives associated with this solicitation necessary to convert the existing space into four exam rooms, a combined waiting/reception area, a relocated police office, and associated support spaces. The general contractor shall furnish all labor, supervision, materials, tools, and equipment necessary to execute the required scope of work. Construction will consist of, but is not limited to, the following: Selective demolition of existing interior partitions, ceilings, finishes, and elements required for new clinic layout. Installation of new interior finishes including flooring, wall finishes, ceilings, trim, and casework. Implementation of therapeutic design features, including calm color schemes, anchored artwork, secure hardware, and achieving a minimum STC-45 acoustic rating for exam room partitions. Installation of new wall-mounted lavatories in each exam room. Routing new domestic hot and cold water from adjacent restrooms and trenching new water lines across the corridor to existing tin-in points. Rebalancing and modifying HVAC systems; reusing the existing rooftop AHU serving the building; relocating or adding diffusers/grilles; installing ligature-resistant diffusers in exam rooms Providing new electrical receptacles, data outlets, and circuits to support clinical functions Installing LED lighting including secured, ligature-resistant fixtures in exam rooms; relocating or supplementing lighting in general spaces; adding occupancy sensors. Removal of existing sprinklers, providing temporary upright sprinkler coverage during construction, and installing new sprinklers to meet NFPA 13 standards Site preparation for installation of Government furnished equipment, including structural supports, utility connections, and required interfaces. Hazardous materials abatement, including asbestos remediation in areas identified during construction; asbestos containing materials are expected in some work areas and must be removed or handled per applicable VA, EPA, OSHA, and state/local regulations. All other items as described in the contract documents. This construction work is located in an occupied, operational clinical facility and must be performed in a manner that allows medical care services to continue uninterrupted throughout construction, This requires carefully phased construction, strict adherence to ICRA, infection control, noise/vibration limits, and daily coordination with the VA COR and end users. Construction may also include the abatement of any asbestos as identified on the provided drawings. The construction of this project will take place in a very busy occupied building and is to be completed to allow medical care functions to be maintained uninterrupted throughout construction necessitating carefully phased construction and coordination with VA COR/users, including strict adherence to ICRA requirements. The estimated project cost range to complete this work is Between $500,000 and $1,000,000. Pursuant to 38 USC 8127(d) and in accordance with Public Law 109-461, the Veterans Benefits, Health Care and Information Technology Act of 2006, this construction project will be solicited as a Total set-aside for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB). The North American Industry Classification Code (NAICS) for this procurement is 236220 Commercial and Institutional Building Construction, with a small business size standard of $45.0 million. Contract Type: Firm Fixed. The duration of the project is estimated to be 210 calendar days from Notice to Proceed. This completion period includes final inspection and cleanup of the premises. Award will be made utilizing Highest technically rated with a fair and reasonable price approach in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation Part 15. Proposal submission instructions will be included in the solicitation package. The government plans to award without discussions. The offeror is responsible to monitor and download any amendments from the Contract Opportunities (https:// sam.gov) website, which may be issued to this solicitation. In accordance with FAR 52.204-7, Required SAM, and in accordance with Veterans Affairs Acquisition Regulation (VAAR) 802.101, prospective contractors must be registered in SAM and in the Veteran Small Business Certification (sba.gov) databases under the applicable NAICS. Firms may obtain SAM information at http://www.sam.gov and Veteran Small Business Certification (sba.gov) information at https://veterans.certify.sba.gov The solicitation package with project specifications and drawings should be available for download on or about September 15, 2026 and the proposal due date will be on or about October 15, 2026. description: Combined Synopsis/Solicitation - 70Z08526Q0027474 The United States Coast Guard Deputy Commandant for Systems (DCS) is issuing this combined synopsis/solicitation on behalf of the Surface Forces Logistics Center (SFLC) to award a firm-fixed-price service contract, as detailed in the attached Statement of Work. The contractor shall provide all labor, supervision, tools, test equipment, incidental materials, travel, and technical support necessary to troubleshoot and repair the Oily Water Separator (OWS) flow totalizer system aboard USCGC POLAR STAR and restore proper receipt, display, and totalization of the overboard flow signal by the PureBilge system. This acquisition is a 100% total small business set-aside under NAICS code 336611 Ship and Boat Building, with a corresponding small business size standard of 1,250 employees. The applicable Product Service Code is J020. All services must be performed on-site at: USCGC POLAR STAR 1519 Alaskan Way S, Seattle, WA 98134 Required period of performance: Work must be completed within 10 days of contract award. The Government will award a contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible offeror whose quote conforming to the solicitation is most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered. The following factors will be used to evaluate offers: � Technical Capability (Pass/Fail) � Past Performance (Pass/Fail) � Total Price A quotation must receive an Acceptable rating for all non-price factors to be eligible for award. Among all acceptable quotations, award will be made to the responsible offeror submitting the lowest evaluated price. To establish Technical Capability (Pass/Fail), the quotation must demonstrate a clear understanding of the work statement requirements, conform strictly to all specifications in the attached Statement of Work, and provide any adequate capability and corporate experience documentation required by the solicitation. Failure to meet these criteria will render the quotation unacceptable. The Government will evaluate recent (completed within the last three years) and relevant past performance to assess the likelihood of successful performance. Past performance will be evaluated on an acceptable or unacceptable basis. To receive an acceptable rating, past performance must demonstrate a rating of satisfactory or higher performance of similar work. Offerors without recent or relevant past performance will be assessed as "Neutral" and considered acceptable for award. Past performance demonstrating marginal or below performance is unacceptable. Offerors shall identify all subcontractors anticipated to perform work under this contract. For each subcontractor, the offeror shall provide the subcontractor�s name, address, point of contact, phone number, the specific work items/specifications they will perform, and the percentage of work they will execute. Submit offers electronically via email to the points of contact identified in this notice. The Government does not prescribe a specific quotation format. Offerors must submit a quotation that clearly identifies the items offered and demonstrates compliance with the stated requirements. Submissions must be complete, clear, and presented in a format that allows effective evaluation by the Government. Submit all questions via email to the points of contact identified in this notice. The Government will not accept telephone inquiries. Submit offers on a firm-fixed-price basis. Prices must be all-inclusive and must cover all costs associated with providing the services, including but not limited to labor, materials, equipment, supervision, transportation, and any other costs. The Government may consider offers nonresponsive if they include conditional pricing, price escalation language, or statements indicating that prices are subject to adjustment based on future costs or fees. The Government intends to evaluate offers and make award without discussions; therefore, offerors should submit their best offer with initial submission. The Statement of Work, market research report, and the list of applicable FAR provisions and clauses are attached to this notice.

title: Z2DA--589A7-23-306 Renovate Bldg. 5 & 5B for Mental Health FY27 NRM
description: Project # 589A7-23-306 Renovate 5 & 5B for Mental Health The Department of Veterans Affairs, Network Contracting Office (NCO) 15, has a requirement for Renovate 5 & 5B for Mental Health, project number 589A7-23-306, located at the U.S Department of Veterans Affairs, Robert J. Dole VA Medical Center 5500 E Kellogg Dr, Wichita, KS 67218 The following narrative is intended to provide an overview of the scope of work for the proposed project. Period of Performance 210 calendar days after Notice to Proceed (NTP) Scope of Work Contractor shall perform construction and renovation of the existing space in Building 5 &/or 5B at the Robert J. Dole VA Medical Center campus. This project will prepare approximately 1,100 SF of existing space in building 5 and/or 5B for use as a same day access mental health clinic in adherence to VHA directive 1231(2) & VHA Handbook 1160.1. This project shall be executed in a manner, following the sequence defined in the design narrative, to maintain continuous operations of adjacent VA clinical functions and medical center functionality throughout construction. All construction work shall be performed in full compliance with the complete set of bidding documents, including all contract drawings, specifications, and design narratives associated with this solicitation necessary to convert the existing space into four exam rooms, a combined waiting/reception area, a relocated police office, and associated support spaces. The general contractor shall furnish all labor, supervision, materials, tools, and equipment necessary to execute the required scope of work. Construction will consist of, but is not limited to, the following: Selective demolition of existing interior partitions, ceilings, finishes, and elements required for new clinic layout. Installation of new interior finishes including flooring, wall finishes, ceilings, trim, and casework. Implementation of therapeutic design features, including calm color schemes, anchored artwork, secure hardware, and achieving a minimum STC-45 acoustic rating for exam room partitions. Installation of new wall-mounted lavatories in each exam room. Routing new domestic hot and cold water from adjacent restrooms and trenching new water lines across the corridor to existing tin-in points. Rebalancing and modifying HVAC systems; reusing the existing rooftop AHU serving the building; relocating or adding diffusers/grilles; installing ligature-resistant diffusers in exam rooms Providing new electrical receptacles, data outlets, and circuits to support clinical functions Installing LED lighting including secured, ligature-resistant fixtures in exam rooms; relocating or supplementing lighting in general spaces; adding occupancy sensors. Removal of existing sprinklers, providing temporary upright sprinkler coverage during construction, and installing new sprinklers to meet NFPA 13 standards Site preparation for installation of Government furnished equipment, including structural supports, utility connections, and required interfaces. Hazardous materials abatement, including asbestos remediation in areas identified during construction; asbestos containing materials are expected in some work areas and must be removed or handled per applicable VA, EPA, OSHA, and state/local regulations. All other items as described in the contract documents. This construction work is located in an occupied, operational clinical facility and must be performed in a manner that allows medical care services to continue uninterrupted throughout construction, This requires carefully phased construction, strict adherence to ICRA, infection control, noise/vibration limits, and daily coordination with the VA COR and end users. Construction may also include the abatement of any asbestos as identified on the provided drawings. The construction of this project will take place in a very busy occupied building and is to be completed to allow medical care functions to be maintained uninterrupted throughout construction necessitating carefully phased construction and coordination with VA COR/users, including strict adherence to ICRA requirements. The estimated project cost range to complete this work is Between $500,000 and $1,000,000. Pursuant to 38 USC 8127(d) and in accordance with Public Law 109-461, the Veterans Benefits, Health Care and Information Technology Act of 2006, this construction project will be solicited as a Total set-aside for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB). The North American Industry Classification Code (NAICS) for this procurement is 236220 Commercial and Institutional Building Construction, with a small business size standard of $45.0 million. Contract Type: Firm Fixed. The duration of the project is estimated to be 210 calendar days from Notice to Proceed. This completion period includes final inspection and cleanup of the premises. Award will be made utilizing Highest technically rated with a fair and reasonable price approach in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation Part 15. Proposal submission instructions will be included in the solicitation package. The government plans to award without discussions. The offeror is responsible to monitor and download any amendments from the Contract Opportunities (https:// sam.gov) website, which may be issued to this solicitation. In accordance with FAR 52.204-7, Required SAM, and in accordance with Veterans Affairs Acquisition Regulation (VAAR) 802.101, prospective contractors must be registered in SAM and in the Veteran Small Business Certification (sba.gov) databases under the applicable NAICS. Firms may obtain SAM information at http://www.sam.gov and Veteran Small Business Certification (sba.gov) information at https://veterans.certify.sba.gov The solicitation package with project specifications and drawings should be available for download on or about September 15, 2026 and the proposal due date will be on or about October 15, 2026. An organized site visit will be scheduled and specific date and time will be made available at time of solicitation issuance. Only one site visit will be scheduled and interested offerors are highly encouraged to attend. No hard copies of the solicitation or drawings will be provided; and telephone requests or questions will NOT be accepted. Please email requests or questions to Jennifer.Hill@va.gov and ensure that the subject line reads "Renovate 5 & 5B for Mental Health, Project Number 589A7-23-306; Solicitation Number: 36C25526R0171

title: Freezer Inventory Software: Freezerworks Base Edition
description: Notice of Intent to Sole Source This is a notice of intent, not a request for a quotation. A solicitation document will not be issued, and quotations will not be requested. The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) intends to negotiate on a sole-source basis with Dataworks Development, Inc., in accordance with FAR 12.102, for Freezer Inventory Software: Freezerworks Base Edition. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition is 513210 � Software Publishers, with a small business size standard of $47.0 million. Background Information and Basis for Sole Source The purpose of this acquisition is to procure the Freezerworks Base Edition software, a comprehensive sample management solution designed for individual teams. This system will replace a legacy homegrown database that is difficult to update and query. The new software will enable real-time monitoring of SRM locations, track temperature excursions, and fulfill the audit requirements of NIST�s quality systems. NIST Materials Measurement Laboratory (MML) has identified Freezerworks Base Edition as the only freezer inventory software that can meet NIST�s requirements. Freezerworks has been in continuous use at the NIST Hollings Marine Laboratory (HML) for their specimen bank since 2010. To maintain uniform inventory control across different NIST locations and minimize potential operational problems, MML must utilize the same software foundation. Using the same software platform across NIST facilities ensures that data structures, metadata fields, and reporting protocols remain consistent. This standardization is critical for the management of SRM inventory that is distributed across multiple locations. Freezerworks also utilizes a proprietary 4D database engine. Dataworks Development, Inc. is the sole author and provider of this architecture, and they are the only entity capable of providing the "Customer Care Program" renewals required for technical support, security patches, and database diagnostics. Further, Dataworks Development Inc. only sells Freezerworks Base Edition software directly to its customers and does not use authorized resellers. Therefore, this is a sole source purchase that the Government must make directly from Dataworks Development, Inc. General No solicitation package will be issued. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive quotations; however, responses received by the listed due date, will be considered by the Government. A determination by the Government not to compete the proposed acquisition based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Interested parties that believe they could satisfy the requirements listed above for NIST may clearly and unambiguously identify their capability to do so in writing on or before the response due date for this notice. This notice of intent is not a solicitation. Any questions regarding this notice must be submitted in writing via email to Anthony Banovic at anthony.banovic@nist.gov. HAARP large scale blast testing and fragmentation characterization
description: Background The Department�s Bureau of Diplomatic Security, Physical Security Division, Research and Development Branch (DS/PSD/RD) is investigating debris generated from perimeter anti-ram barriers during a Vehicle Borne Improvised Explosive Device (VBIED) attack. DS/PSD/RD is seeking proposals to conduct large scale blast testing and fragmentation tracking. Government Furnished Information to Performer: DOS DS PSD Standard Practice for Blast Tests Final report and test data from previous anti-ram barrier debris characterization testing Physical Security Handbook (Red Book) drawing templates Scope This effort will be broken into two phases. Phase 1 will be to evaluate and characterize the debris generated from a simulated VBIED attack against baseline Department anti-ram systems, identified in this document. Phase 2 will be to evaluate and characterize debris generated from modified Department anti-ram systems. Performers will be evaluated on: Ability to perform testing in accordance with Blast Testing SOP for DS/PSP/PSD Responders shall provide a narrative for test site setup as part of performer evaluation. Test facility capabilities: Topography suitable for instrumentation Large, clear, flat, and level test spaces are ideal to best characterize the debris: Ability to characterize dynamic debris at 75ft, 100ft, 200ft, and 300ft Ability to character debris at rest post test (as far as 1,500ft from initial test article location) Free of debris from previous tests Widths that can accommodate HS camera views that capture overall events A 2,000 lbs. TNT NEW range limit is the minimum required to conduct this testing. DS/PSD/RD will accept either single test article test, or if appropriate, test two test articles simultaneously as seen in Figure 1: Will require larger test range, ~3,000ft Figure 1: Example of Setup to Test Two Anti-Ram Fences in One Test Instrumentation plan: Required to characterize debris generated from the anti-ram barriers: At 75ft, 100ft, 200ft, 300ft, and at rest Characterize the following from debris: Dimensions Weight Velocity Height from ground Dispersion Plan to differentiate debris from one test to the next (concrete dye, paint, etc.) and/or clear range of debris from prior tests DS/PSD/RD has no prescribed methodology to capture the above data; The performer shall propose their instrumentation and post processing plans including the types of data acquisition equipment and any software needed to do the analysis. Schedule: Complete the project within 24 months, with more consideration given to condensed schedules. Compressed testing dates are preferred to avoid excess testing travel lengths or multiple trips. DS/PSD/RD Understands cost and schedule need to be balanced. Testing two anti-ram fences simultaneously saves time, explosives, and setup labor but requires duplicate instrumentation and a much larger test range. Performer should provide their plan and justify. Performer is also welcome to provide several; approaches and let DS/PSD/RD decide which is most advantageous to the government. Phase 1: Initial Anti-Ram Barrier Debris Characterization: Set up: For planning purposes, the surrogate Vehicle Borne Improvised Explosive Device will be a charge with the NEW of 2,000lbs TNT, in a cylinder with a L/D of 1, sat atop a 32in table, centered on a 10ft x 10ft concrete pad, and placed so that there is a 24in gap between the edge of charge and the test article. The boundary conditions of the test articles will influence the amount of debris generated during the testing, but the government needs to balance cost with real world simulation. Therefore, the government would like the performer to provide options to build and test the test articles in lengths of 30ft, 45ft and 60ft long sections and constructed per the drawings in Appendix A. Figure 2: Example Test Article Layout Phase 1 Test Articles: Test Sample Design Being Tested Drawings in Appendix B Brief Description (See Appendix A for Details) Potential to Combine tests Length of Test sample Options Base 1 AC-41-05 Bar Fence on top of DS-50 Knee Wall 20x20mm Bars @ 65mm OC N B1.1: 30ft B1.2: 45ft B1.3:60ft Base 2 AC-41-06 Picket Fence on top of DS-50 Knee Wall 50mm x 6mm Pickets @200mm OC N B2.1: 30ft B2.2: 45ft B2.3:60ft Base 3 DS-40 Anti- Climb & Ram Fence 20x20mm Bars @ 130 mm OC w/ DN250 XS Pipes @ 1,720mm OC Yes w/ base 4 or Option 2 B3.1: 30ft B3.2: 45ft B3.3:60ft Base 4 DS-44 Steel Anti- Climb & Ram Fence 100mm x 50mm x 6mm Tubes @ 175mm OC Yes w/ base 3 or Option 2 B4.1: 30ft B4.2: 45ft B4.3:60ft Option 1 AC-41-04 Tube Fence on top of DS-50 Knee Wall 38mm dia. x 3mm Tubes @150mm OC N O1.1: 30ft O1.2: 45ft O1.3:60ft Option 2 DS-43 Steel Anti- Climb & Ram Fence with Kickers 100mm x 50mm x 6mm Tubes @ 175mm OC with Kickers @ 350mm OC Yes w/ base 2 or base 3 O2.1: 30ft O2.2: 45ft O2.3:60ft After the Phase 1 test data will be analyzed by the performer and DS/PSD will determine which test samples produced the most and least hazardous fragmentation based of level of hazardous debris produced. Phase 2: Modified Anti-Ram Barrier Debris Characterization: In certain scenarios the Department requires perimeters to employ opaque barriers to prevent easy external observation. To meet this requirement the test samples that produced the least hazardous fragmentation in Phase 1 will be fitted with various opaque claddings and tested to determine which produce the least hazardous fragmentation. The performer will research various opaque claddings that will provide concealment with preference to those that would mitigate and reduce the level of hazardous debris generated. The performer will research and propose feasible fence and knee-wall cladding materials that can be tested in Phase 2. The criteria for potential fence cladding are: Opaque Weather resistant Aesthetically pleasing Potential to break up in a non-hazardous way Large yet low mass pieces Small pieces Consumed by VBIED�s thermal energy Etc. Readily available construction materials Cost effective and easily constructable Test Sample Design Being Tested Example Cladding Options will be Researched and Suggested by Performer and Accepted by DS/PSD/RD Potential to Combine tests Length of Test sample Options Option 3 Best Performing Fence on knee wall with opaque cladding E.g.: 24-gauge stainless steel 316L or Alum equivalent decorative panel on fence and steel plate behind knee wall N O3.1: 30ft O3.2: 45ft O3.3:60ft Option 4 Best Performing Fence on knee wall with opaque cladding E.g.: Metal plate material on fence and knee wall N O4.1: 30ft O4.2: 45ft O4.3:60ft Option 5 Best Performing Anti-Ram Fence with Opaque cladding E.g.: Stainless steel 316L or Alum equivalent decorative panel on fence Yes w/ Option 6 O5.1: 30ft O5.2: 45ft O5.3:60ft Option 6 Best Performing Anti-Ram Fence with Opaque cladding E.g.: Light weight material Yes w/ Option 5 O6.1: 30ft O6.2: 45ft O6.3:60ft Deliverables Test Data: The performer will determine the best method to place video cameras, gauges, surveying equipment, etc. necessary to capture the desired data. The performer shall present their instrumentation plan to DS for feedback and approval prior to the test. Dynamic data to be collected is as follows: HS Video: Overall Event and downrange point of view (e.g. at 1,000ft) At 75ft, 100ft, 200ft and 300ft Dimension/description of debris (steel, concrete, steel and concrete, etc.) At 75ft, 100ft, 200ft, and 300ft Estimated weight of debris At 75ft, 100ft, 200ft, and 300ft Velocity of debris At 75ft, 100ft, 200ft and 300ft Height of debris At 75ft, 100ft, 200ft, and 300ft Dispersion pattern of debris At 75ft, 100ft, 200ft, and 300ft Post blast debris assessment will be conducted to characterize the debris. The performer shall determine the search area necessary to capture 90% of the debris weighing one pound or more (estimated to be 1,000ft to 1,500ft from originating position but performer needs to confirm). description: Description: The Royal Canadian Mounted Police in Arviat and Cambridge Bay, Nunavut Territories, has a requirement for the Supply and Delivery of Mechanical Maintenance Services at the RCMP Arviat Detachment and Cambridge Bay Detachment. This procurement is subject to the Nunavut Land Claims Agreement and the Directive on Government Contracts, Including Real Property Leases, in the Nunavut Settlement Area. Bidders are requested to maximize Inuit employment, subcontracting and on-the-job training opportunities, and involve Inuit businesses, in carrying out the work under this project. The Nunavut Agreement contains a provision requiring the inclusion of socio-economic bid criteria in the solicitation document, when practicable and consistent with sound procurement management principles. These socio-economic bid criteria are referred to as Nunavut Benefits Criteria (NBC) and Inuit Benefits Criteria (IBC), and bidders propose Inuit benefits in their bid submission via an Inuit Benefits Plan (IBP). This solicitation is limited for bidding among firms registered on the Inuit Firm Registry (IFR). Bids submitted by businesses not on the IFR will render the bid non-responsive and no further consideration will be accorded to the bid. Policy on Reciprocal Procurement This solicitation of bids is open only to Canadian suppliers and to Suppliers of an applicable trading partner. Delivery Date: The contract period will be for 12-months from the date of contract. Security: This requirement contains a security requirement. Basis of selection: A bid must comply with all the requirements of the bid solicitation and meet all mandatory requirements. Bids not meeting the requirements will be declared non-responsive. The selection will be based on the highest responsive combined rating of total Inuit Benefits Plan (IBP) merit, technical merit and price. The ratio will be 30% for the total IBP merit, 30 % for the technical merit and 40% for price. Tenders must be submitted to the RCMP Bid Receiving Unit at: NWR_Procurement_Bids@rcmp-grc.gc.ca Refer to the attached tender documents to obtain further information. Canada retains the right to negotiate with any supplier on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. The RCMP has adopted the Integrity Regime administered by Public Services and Procurement Canada. As a result, the integrity provisions are being applied in RCMP contracting activities as outlined in this solicitation. Canada will make available Notices of Proposed Procurement (NPP), bid solicitations and related documents for download through the Government Electronic Tendering Service (GETS) at https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities . Canada is not responsible and will not assume any liabilities whatsoever for the information found on websites of third parties. In the event an NPP, bid solicitation or related documentation would be amended, Canada will not be sending notifications. Canada will post all amendments, including significant enquiries received and their replies, using GETS. It is the sole responsibility of the Bidder to regularly consult GETS for the most up-to-date information. Canada will not be liable for any oversight on the Bidder's part nor for notification services offered by a third party. Indigenous Procurement: The federal Indigenous Business Directory (IBD) is an online resource for all levels of government and the private sector to identify Indigenous business capacity. Having a business profile in the IBD will increase your company’s visibility and may provide additional business. A profile in the IBD can also allow you to compete for federal government contracts that are set-aside for Indigenous businesses through the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Businesses. For more information and to review eligibility criteria and register, visit: www.canada.ca/indigenousbusinessdirectory.

title: Germany – Accumulators, primary cells and primary batteries – Batteriespeicher BESS II Harrislee
description: Gegenstand des vorliegenden Projektes ist die Errichtung und der Betrieb eines netzgekoppelten Stand-Alone-Batteriespeichersystems (BESS) mit einer elektrischen Anschlussleistung von 70 MW sowie einer nutzbaren Speicherkapazität von 140 MWh auf dem Betriebsgelände des Kunden. Das Speichersystem soll über einen Mittelspannungstransformator an das kundeneigene 60 kV-Mittelspannungsnetz angebunden werden und dient der Teilnahme am Arbitragehandel. Der Aufstellungsort des Batteriespeichers befindet sich auf einer grünen Wiese, dessen im Besitz der STADTWERKE FLENSBURG GMBH (SWFL) liegt. Die Ausführung des Systems ist als containerisierte bzw. modulare Speicherlösung vorgesehen, bestehend aus Batteriesystemen, Wechselrichtereinheiten, Transformatorentechnik, Schutz- und Leittechnik sowie den erforderlichen Nebenanlagen. Die Speicherkapazität soll zur Teilnahme am Energiehandel eingesetzt werden. Vorgesehen ist insbesondere die Vermarktung von Flexibilitäten über kurzfristige Strommärkte, um Erlöse aus Price Spreads und marktbedingten Arbitragepotenzialen zu generieren. Darüber hinaus soll das Batteriespeichersystem zur Bereitstellung von Sekundärregelleistung (aFRR) eingesetzt werden und somit zusätzliche Erlöse aus der Teilnahme am Regelenergiemarkt erzielen. Durch den marktorientierter Mehrfachnutzung wird eine wirtschaftlich optimierte Betriebsweise des Speichersystems angestrebt.

title: Ireland – Electrical engineering installation works – TII522 Electrical Renewals Works (Low Voltage) IMPQQ
description: TII intends to enter into Multi Party Framework Agreement for Luas Electrical Renewals and Upgrade Works (Low Voltage) for the Luas Light Rail System. This IMPQQ competition aims to identify and shortlist highly qualified electrical contractors with proven electrical expertise and experience in Low Voltage (LV) electrical systems for light rail or heavy rail infrastructure, specifically in the design, installation, testing, commissioning, and compliance of railway electrical systems at LV level. This framework, when established, will be available to TII to draw down from it on a CallOff Contract basis, (PW-CF2 and PW-CF4). The Applicant must demonstrate a strong track record of delivering complex electrical works in live operational rail environments, ensuring safety, quality, reliability, and full regulatory compliance. The Applicant must demonstrate their experience in the design, installation, testing, commissioning of safetycritical electrical systems in live railway environments and compliance of various railway electrical LV systems. Applicants must demonstrate their experience working in live railway environment and must be capable of acting as the Project Supervisor for the Design Process (PSDP) and the Project Supervisor for the Construction Stage (PSCS) in accordance with Irish health and safety legislation. TII are inviting expressions of interest from interested parties to be selected to tender with a view to entering into the Contract. Applicants are referred to the Information Memorandum and Prequalification Questionnaire (IMPQQ) which provides additional information in relation to the competition. Provided that there is a sufficient number of suitable Applicants, TII intends to invite the number of Applicants (as indicated in this IMPQQ) to tender. Prior to shortlisting any Applicant, TII reserves the right to seek verification of any declarations made in the response to the ESPD/IMPQQ.

description: THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE PURCHASE ORDER WITHOUT PROVIDING FOR FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION OR A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. GENERAL This notice is issued in accordance with Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) 12.201-1(c)(2), advertising the Government's intent to issue an award on a sole source basis under the authority established in RFO 12.102(a). The National Institutes of Health, Specialized Scientific Information Technology (SSIT) Division anticipates issuing a single Purchase Order (PO) to the following entity: PROLIFIC ACADEMIC LTD 483 Green Lanes London, N13 4BS United Kingdom BACKGROUND Researchers within the Division of Population Health Research of the Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development (NICHD) require services from an online recruitment platform to support behavioral nutrition studies with English-speaking adults. The studies require recruiting participants from specific populations, including adults, parents of young children, and U.S. residents. Access to a separate online participant pool, distinct from those used in other phases of the research, is required to maintain the scientific integrity of the research, as recruiting participants from the same pool across study phases would compromise the study design by increasing the likelihood of prior exposure to study materials and repeat participation. This platform must meet the following requirements: The platform must be designed specifically to support research studies rather than general crowdsourcing activities for which research is only a secondary use. The platform must allow researchers to estimate, prior to recruitment, the number of active participants available who meet specified eligibility criteria, including demographic, geographic, language, and behavioral characteristics. The platform must support longitudinal research by enabling researchers to re-contact and re-recruit participants for follow-up surveys and assessments. The platform must allow researchers to directly determine participant compensation rates for individual studies. The platform must support rapid recruitment of participants, including the ability to recruit hundreds of eligible participants within days to weeks. The platform must allow researchers to review study completion status and directly approve participant compensation. The platform must support collection of high-quality research data through participant screening, participant management, and data quality controls. Based on market research, only Prolific is capable of providing access to the Prolific participant pool and associated participant recruitment platform, which offers data collection from a wide participant pool of primarily English-speaking adults that is more cost-effective and efficient than other vendors. No third-party vendor can provide access to the Prolific participant pool or replicate the platform's participant prescreening and recruitment infrastructure. Therefore, only one source is available to furnish these services. RESPONSES There will not be a solicitation or competitive Request for Quotation (RFQ) issued as a result of this announcement. Any responses or inquiries to this notice must demonstrate clear and convincing evidence that competition will be advantageous to the Government. Notwithstanding the stated intent, if other organizations believe they can fully meet the Government�s requirement, they must submit written documentation of their capabilities. The capabilities statement must contain sufficient documentation to establish a bona fide capability to fulfill the requirement and must be received by the response date listed in this posting. A general statement which merely states the entity is capable will not be sufficient. A determination not to compete with this requirement, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the Government. NIH will not be responsible for any costs incurred by interested parties in responding to this notice. Acknowledgement of receipt of responses will not be made, nor will respondents be notified of the evaluation of the information received. Interested parties may respond and provide a capability statement no later than the date specified in this notice. Emails must reference the announcement number in the subject line. This is not an RFQ, and this announcement does not commit the Government to award a contract.

title: Procurement of two (2) fully trained Border Collies from Kuykendall Border Collies, LLC to Perform Wildlife Damage Management for the Hokuala Resort K9 Project
description: SOLE SOURCE Procurement of two (2) fully trained Border Collies from Kuykendall Border Collies, LLC to Perform Wildlife Damage Management for the Hokuala Resort K9 Project Project H?k?ala Resort K9 Hazing Project General Information 1.0 Scope of Work Provide a brief statement of the overall project, including goals and objectives. The H?k?ala Resort is a property adjacent to Lihue Airport, the Part-139 airport servicing the island of Kauai. The presence of the Hawaiian goose or n?n? (Branta sandvicensis) poses considerable bird aircraft strike hazard risk to the daily operations at the airport, threatening human health and safety. The mission of the H?k?ala Resort K9 Hazing Project is to reduce the presence and numbers of n?n? using the land and airspace surrounding the airport to increase traveler safety and minimize property damage costs. Border collies are the only K9 approved by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service to perform hazing actions on the n?n?. Because of the optics and restrictions of the popular and heavily trafficked H?k?ala Resort, traditional hazing methods are not approved for use on the property. Contractor Requirements 3.0 Technical Requirements / Tasks USDA Wildlife Services Hawai`i requests a single source vendor for the acquisition of two American Border Collie Association (ABCA) certified and trained K9s. Please see the Justification for Other than Full and Open Competition (JOFOC), Attachment A and Attachment B. Per the U. S. Fish and Wildlife Service Environmental Assessment for the H?k?ala Resort project, ABCA certified and trained K9s only are approved for hazing the ESA-listed n?n?. Because Hawai�i is rabies free, there is State of Hawai`i law requiring a rabies titer be conducted on the K9 120 days before it can be admitted into the state. Additionally, the K9s require a health certificate specific to Hawai`i. Border collies shall be fully trained as goose-dogs, with a strong desire to work and the ability to work long hours. The Border collies shall be of stable temperament, with ready response to voice and whistle commands; they shall be socialized to the public. The Border collies shall have experience and training in both pastures and water and shall have both firearm and pyrotechnic desensitization. The Border collies shall also be trained to operate out of both golf carts and vehicles. Additional requirements can be found in Attachment C. 4.0 Government Furnished N/A 5.0 Deliverables / Schedule K9s shall be procured by August 1, 2026 with arrival to the island of Kauai, HI prior to the beginning of the breeding season (September 2026). 6.0 Travel Identify any travel requirements, locations involved, number of trips (if known), and duration of anticipated travel. Specify responsibility for travel reimbursement, e.g., the contractor or the Government. If the travel will be reimbursed by the Government, discuss the method of reimbursement, e.g., in accordance with Federal/agency travel regulations. State the Government official authorized to approve contractor travel, e.g., the Contracting Officer or Contracting Officer Representative. USDA Wildlife Services K9 handlers shall travel to North Carolina for five days of training on site with the Kuykendalls. During this time, handlers will learn the key skills to successfully work with the ABCA-certified border collies, as well as begin bonding with their assigned K9 before returning to Kauai with their K9. Travel requirements have been separately budgeted into the work financial plan for the Hokuala Resort K9 Hazing Project. Contracting Officer: Todd K. title: 535TRS M4 TRAINER WEAPONS
description: The 502d Contracting Squadron, Joint Base San Antonio-Lackland (JBSA-Lackland), TX intends to solicit and award a sole-source, firm-fixed-price purchase order to Laser Shot, Inc. under the authority of RFO 6.103-1(a) (10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) or 41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(1)). This requirement is for three hundred and fifty (350) M4 Trainer Weapons for the 535th Training Squadron at JBSA-Lackland, TX. Through market research, the Laser Shot M4 Trainer Weapons are determined to be essential to the Government's requirements to maintain absolute instructional continuity and direct compatibility with the existing training inventory, technical manuals, and established Basic Military Training (BMT) curriculum. Laser Shot, Inc. holds the exclusive proprietary manufacturing and design rights for this M4 Trainer Weapon (acquired from Olympic Arms, Inc.), does not utilize authorized resellers or distributors, and is the sole manufacturer of these devices. No other product can meet the training squadron safety and instructional requirements without unacceptable training inconsistencies, duplication of cost, and schedule delays. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 332994 (Small Arms, Ordnance, and Ordnance Accessories Manufacturing), with a small business size standard of 1,000 employees. This NAICS code is selected because the M4 Trainer Weapons are structurally inert replica firearms manufactured utilizing actual firearm fabrication processes, tooling, and materials to prevent live-fire conversion. If an interested party believes this NAICS code is incorrect, please provide your recommended NAICS code with a supporting rationale in your response. This NOTICE OF INTENT is not a Solicitation or a Request for Quote. It is a Government notification of the intent to proceed with a Sole-Source acquisition. However, interested parties who believe they can fulfill this requirement may submit a capability statement and past performance narrative. Submissions must clearly demonstrate the capability to provide inert M4 training weapons that possess the standard 10-part field-strip mechanical disassembly realism and a certified, unrestricted, arms-room-free ATF-exempt training status. All capability statements must be submitted via email in response to this notice.

title: Aqualab VSA Vapor Sorption Analyzer
description: The USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) on behalf of USDA Agricultural Research Service intends to award a firm-fixed price purchase order on a sole source basis to Addium, Inc (1300 NE Henley Court, Ste. 6, Pullman WA 99163-56662) for the procurement of (1) Aqualab VSA Vapor Sorption Analyzer Part #40430; (1) VSA Service Training Part #50194; (1) Aqualab WVTR Testing Kit Part #40237; (1) Moisture Analysis Toolkit 3.0 Part #50229; (1) Aqualab Stainless Steel Cups Part #40314; and shipping if applicable. Statutory Authority This purchase is being conducted under the authority of FAR 12. The FSIS has determined that Addium, Inc. is the only source reasonably available to satisfy this requirement of the Aqualab VSA Vapor Sorption Analyzer from Addium, Inc. because of their unique capabilities exclusive to their product. The Aqualab VSA can perform dynamic dewpoint isotherms, which is proprietary. Unlike the conventional dynamic vapor sorption isotherm method, dynamic dewpoint isotherms are independent of sample equilibration for setting water activities, allowing for increased precision and detection of inflection points in isotherm curves indicative of critical relative humidities. This would allow us to determine appropriate storage conditions that do not lead to migration of components and deterioration in product quality, such as with sugar blooming. Since this is a proprietary method, no other vapor sorption analyzer on the market has these capabilities. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. It�s a synopsis for informational purposes only. However, any responsible source that believes it can meet this requirement may submit a capability statement, which shall be considered by the agency. Responses must include: 1. Company Name and CAGE Code. 2. Technical description of how the proposed alternative meets all requirements listed above. Responses will be used to determine if a competitive procurement is necessary, at the discretion of the Contracting Officer.

title: TYPE 3 FIRE ENGINES
description: The U. S. Forest Service (USFS) is soliciting a proposal from qualified vendors for sixteen (16) Type 3 fire engines, body only configuration, to be installed on Government-furnished 4X2 and 4X4 cab and chassis. Scope includes chassis modifications and preparation, installation of the body, fire pump, 600-gallon water tank, warning lights, required graphics package, and all components necessary to deliver a complete operational unit. Apparatus must meet Forest Service national standard specifications, including compliance with NFPA 1900 unless otherwise specified. Proposal shall include delivery of each unit and on-site familiarization training. Vendors shall demonstrate their capability to produce apparatus meeting the requirements of the USFS, summarized in executive form.
